## Published Papers

<div class="paper-entry">
  <div class="paper-title">Financial structure and mergers</div>
  <div class="paper-authors">Charles Taragin, Benjamin Wallace, and Eddie Watkins</div>
  <div class="paper-venue">International Journal of Industrial Organization, 107: 103302 (2026)</div>
  <div class="paper-contribution">Studies how corporate debt influences the competitive outcomes of horizontal and conglomerate mergers. Shows that mergers can spread fixed debt obligations across a broader product portfolio, creating an "insurance effect" against adverse demand shocks that interacts with the traditional recapture effect from reduced competition.</div>
  <div class="paper-links">
  <a href="https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijindorg.2026.103302" target="_blank"><i class="fas fa-external-link-alt"></i> DOI</a>
  <a href="https://github.com/luciu5/MergerDebt" target="_blank"><i class="fab fa-github"></i> Code</a>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="paper-entry">
  <div class="paper-title">A distance-based algorithm for defining antitrust markets</div>
  <div class="paper-authors">Charles Taragin and Marco Taylhardat</div>
  <div class="paper-venue">Finance Research Letters, 86: 108972 (2025)</div>
  <div class="paper-contribution">Develops a distance-based approach to geographic market definition, with direct relevance for merger screening and regulated-market analysis.</div>
  <div class="paper-links">

</div>

<div class="paper-entry">
  <div class="paper-title">Consequences of model choice in predicting horizontal merger effects</div>
  <div class="paper-authors">Matthew T. Panhans and Charles Taragin</div>
  <div class="paper-venue">International Journal of Industrial Organization, 89: 102986 (2023)</div>
  <div class="paper-contribution">Shows how predicted merger effects can differ across plausible conduct models, making model uncertainty a first-order issue in merger simulation.</div>
  <div class="paper-links">

  </div>
</div>
